entrypoints.summary: A first-factor-authenticated client submits a four-digit mfa-code parameter to POST /login2.

negative_controls: Wrong code entered twice causes logout according to the lab instructions.
The verification code may reset during the enumeration, requiring the procedure to be repeated.
observability.positive_marker: HTTP 302 from one POST /login2 candidate request.

preconditions: Possession of the target user's valid username and password.
No access to the target user's current 2FA verification code.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Valid target username and password, followed by the second-factor challenge flow.
trigger_steps.summary: Establish or renew the first-factor-authenticated state using GET /login, POST /login, and GET /login2.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Every four-digit zero-padded integer from 0000 to 9999, one concurrent request.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit sequential candidate values to the mfa-code parameter on POST /login2.

mitigations.concept: Aggregate 2FA verification-attempt bound across renewed sessions

relation_candidates.rationale: The lab begins with valid victim credentials and directs the resulting logged-in client to POST a candidate mfa-code to the second-factor endpoint.
The lab directs submission of every four-digit candidate to the mfa-code parameter, renewing the login session before each request after incorrect-code logout.
The documented 0–9999 enumeration reports a 302 on a successful request and then access to My account.

relation_candidates.dst: Aggregate 2FA verification-attempt bound across renewed sessions
relation_candidates.rationale: The source does not prescribe a remediation; this relationship is an explicitly inferred control needed to stop the documented re-login-per-attempt enumeration path.

impact.affected_asset: Carlos's account page and the account's authenticated web-session access.
impact.attacker_capability: An actor with the valid first-factor credentials can obtain authenticated access without possession of the verification code by enumerating its four-digit value.
impact.security_effect: Bypass of the intended two-factor authentication check for the targeted account.

causal_trace.summary: The attacker has valid Carlos username/password credentials but lacks the user's 2FA verification code.

The lab identifies the two-factor authentication mechanism as vulnerable to brute-forcing; incorrect-code logout after two attempts can be bypassed operationally by automatically re-establishing the first-factor session before each candidate submission.
The attacker submits every zero-padded four-digit integer from 0000 through 9999 as the mfa-code value to POST /login2, with one concurrent request.
A request returning HTTP 302 identifies a successful verification-code guess and enables access to Carlos's account page.

failure.operation: POST /login2 verification of attacker-controlled mfa-code candidates

primary_invariant.statement: A party possessing only the first authentication factor must not be able to obtain second-factor authentication by exhaustively submitting the finite verification-code space across renewed login sessions.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The supplied lab procedure renews the Carlos login session before each POST /login2 attempt and enumerates all four-digit code candidates until a 302 response is observed.

quality.review_notes: This is a PortSwigger instructional lab, not a production advisory or code/patch review. The page gives an explicit request sequence, candidate range, and HTTP success marker, but the verification code can reset during an attack, so the documented procedure may require repetition. No source-backed remediation patch, implementation source, or execution transcript is present; the remediation class is explicitly inference.

remediation.invariant_restored: The supplied material does not document a remediation or patch. A mitigation would need to prevent exhaustive mfa-code enumeration from continuing merely by obtaining a new first-factor session.
mitigation_classes: aggregate bounding of 2FA verification attempts across reauthenticated sessions (inferred mitigation)

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Observed 2026-07-16; no explicit release, version, or commit is published

target.project_or_package: PortSwigger Web Security Academy 2FA brute-force lab

oracle.expected_negative: Incorrect code submissions do not return the documented 302 success indicator; the lab notes that two wrong codes log the client out.
oracle.expected_positive: One enumerated four-digit mfa-code request returns HTTP 302, after which the response URL can be loaded and My account accessed.
